---
title: "About"
---

I am from Hanoi, spent college in Appleton, Wisconsin, and am heading to Tallahassee to start an Economics PhD at Florida State. Somewhere in that triangle I picked up an interest in applied microeconomics, political economy, housing markets, and the statistical computing needed to make empirical work less hand-wavy.

Last summer, I worked as a research fellow under Prof. Andrew Sage in collaboration with [Fox Valley Data Exchange](https://www.fvdex.org/). We worked on public-health data infrastructure for the Fox Valley area: assembling indicators, thinking through missingness and interpolation, and making the output legible enough to be useful outside a statistics classroom. That work has continued into the school year as an internship in public health data.

My capstone asks whether general elections distort housing transaction volumes. Using state-level monthly pending home sales from 2012 to 2025, I compare presidential and midterm cycles against non-election seasonal baselines. The broad result is suggestive: presidential elections seem to suppress pending sales before Election Day, while the expected post-election release of demand is much less obvious.

Current interests:

- applied microeconomics
- political economy
- experimental and behavioral economics
- housing markets
- statistical computing
